summary: NVMe checkpoint write stall during background model snapshot causing elevated 5xx for Peregrine AI on Dedicated us-west-2
description:
Issue summary: Beginning ~2026-02-18T12:10Z Peregrine AI reported elevated 5xx rates on generation and embedding routes. Impact: customer-facing errors and degraded throughput for a single Dedicated cluster serving Peregrine. Environment: Dedicated pool in us-west-2 backing Peregrine AI (multi-tenant node group with host-local NVMe).

Observed behaviour: API Gateway returned 502/520/503 for ~15-30s bursts; upstream runtimes showed long blocking syscalls and unresponsive worker threads. Customer observed failed embedding uploads and increased tail latency.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Large background model snapshot/sanity-check was kicked on a host with active tenant traffic. 2) Concurrent embedding bursts from customer (~10k small requests/min) ran while snapshot wrote model checkpoints to local NVMe. 3) System entered accept-queue growth, proxied connections hit timeouts and API gateway 5xx responses.

Initial hypothesis: Storage IO stall (NVMe) from large checkpoint write combined with scheduler preemption caused runtime worker threads to block leading to upstream unavailability and API gateway 5xx amplification.
investigation_notes:
- Correlated API gateway traces with node-level iostat and strace on the runtime.
- NVMe device on node ip-10-48-23-11 reported long latencies (avg 900ms for write ops) coincident with checkpoint duration.
- runtimes showed threads stuck in fsync() and write() syscalls; kernel stack samples show I/O wait.
- Snapshot service launched without write-throttling; snapshot size ~45GB and peak write bandwidth saturated local NVMe queue.
- Scheduler placed additional tenant prefetch jobs onto the same host during snapshot window; acceptance queue grew and proxy timeouts increased.
- No immediate software crash; runtime threads were blocked leading to connection timeouts and API gateway surfaced 5xx.
- NVMe SMART reported intermittent reallocated sectors and firmware revision older than recommended.

Evidence artifacts: Attached traces (internal links) and apigw logs; referenced in Confluence runbook for storage stalls.
timeline: 2026-02-18T12:08Z - Peregrine alerts sent to support Slack #support-peregrine
2026-02-18T12:10Z - Spike in 5xx observed in prod us-west-2; support paging on-call SRE
2026-02-18T12:15Z - SRE confirmed NVMe high write latency on host ip-10-48-23-11
2026-02-18T12:20Z - Snapshot interrupted via scheduler cancel; immediate drop in NVMe latency observed
2026-02-18T12:34Z - API 5xx rates return to baseline; customer notified of mitigation steps
2026-02-20T09:00Z - Firmware upgrade scheduled and host replaced from Dedicated pool; ticket moved to Resolved
comments: Maya Chen (Support): Received initial report from customer; opened incident and escalated to SRE. Notified account team.
Arjun Patel (SRE): Observed blocked threads in runtime and high nvme write latencies. Suspected long-running snapshot without IO shaping.
Lena Kostova (Infra): Confirmed NVMe SMART counters showing reallocated sectors; recommended host replacement and firmware update.

Customer (Peregrine AI - ops@peregrine.ai): Provided traffic patterns and confirmed scheduled internal snapshot at ~12:05Z (misaligned with high traffic window). Appreciative of quick mitigation; requested root-cause analysis.
Arjun Patel (SRE): Applied immediate mitigation: cancelled snapshot job, drained affected host, and moved Peregrine traffic to healthy hosts. Posted temporary workaround to customer.
root_cause: A large background model checkpoint wrote directly to local NVMe without IO throttling while the device exhibited degraded health/older firmware. The unshaped write saturated device queues and caused runtime worker threads to block on write/fsync calls, creating upstream unavailability and resulting in API gateway 5xx amplification.
workaround: Cancelled the running snapshot and drained the affected host out of the Dedicated pool. Temporarily pinned Peregrine traffic to alternate hosts and advised customer to postpone heavy snapshot activity during peak traffic windows.
resolution_notes:
Fixes applied: 1) Replaced the degraded NVMe host and applied recommended firmware. 2) Deployed snapshot IO-shaper in scheduler to cap per-host checkpoint write bandwidth (default 150 MB/s) and added random jitter to snapshot start times. 3) Updated Dedicated runbook to avoid scheduling snapshots during peak customer traffic windows and to detect NVMe SMART thresholds that trigger host evacuation. 4) Added alerting in storage-monitoring to detect per-host sustained write latency >200ms.

Customer communication: Notified Peregrine AI of root cause, mitigations, and completed remediation. No billing adjustments requested. Customer acknowledged and closed follow-up call on 2026-02-19.
postmortem_actions: Scheduler: Implement IO-shaper for background snapshot tasks (owner: infra/scheduler) - done
Monitoring: Create alert for sustained host write latency >200ms (owner: observability) - done
Infra: Audit NVMe firmware across Dedicated fleet and schedule bulk firmware updates (owner: infra) - in progress
Runbook: Add a preflight snapshot check to ensure host write health and traffic low-watermark (owner: SRE) - done
Customer Ops: Update customer onboarding guidance for snapshot windows and recommended snapshot sizing (owner: CS) - done
